Same data in both views? Both read the one session file that Servex writes: Servex/agents/Sessions.js:613 write() appends it and pushes the SSE. The first view (ux/Dictate/chat.js) gets lines from Session.watch(file) and Session.stream(session) at chat.js:269 and :276. Chat v2 gets the same file through ext/drawer/ChatView.js:52 new ChatV2({url:file}) -> ext/Chat/v2/ChatV2.js:28 -> ext/JSONL/JSONL.js:55 (dev socket). The assistants write nothing themselves; Servex writes their lines. They differ in what they fold: chat.js draw_line (:212) drops any line that is not chat/refined/para/place/sent/summary/react, e.g. an edit-by-id Question line, while ChatV2Model.fold sees every line.

Q1 marks. The mic icon is the via badge: ext/Chat/Chat.js:46-51 via_badge, drawn from the line's via (voice shows the mic with tooltip 'said', typed shows 'typed'). The green check IS the clarity mark and it is live: ux/Dictate/chat.js:163 sets marks:true; Widget.js:596 Thread.mark posts each new owner line (not history) to /api/hitl op marks (Servex/Servex.js:734, Servex/agents/Hitl.js:16-23, a small no-tools model call: ok = reads as clear, unclear = a real fork in meaning, lenient by design) and patch_piece stores it; Chat.js:108-113 mark_badge draws a check (chatbox-mark-ok) or a ? (chatbox-mark-unclear) with the model's purpose as the tooltip. The ? in my proof screenshot is the stubbed /api/hitl answering unclear. The model also returns a `question` with two readings for an unclear line, but nothing draws it. The old v1 thread has the same call at Widget.js:202.

Q2 server state. Yes: Servex/agents/Sessions.js:227 `export default class Sessions` is one instance holding every voice session's state (constructor :229, defaults() :232 holds map, by_agent, held, floor_timers, thoughts, clients, buffers at :247-248), persisted to sessions.json (load :472, save()). A single session is a plain record object `s` made at :798 ({id, home, file, kind:'voice', fast, smart, ...}), not its own class; the behaviour lives in Sessions methods (say, hold_thought :1104, release_thought :1116, write :613, feed_smart :265), and WakePolicy (Servex/agents/WakePolicy.js:24) is a second small class for the smart seat's timing, one instance (`waker`, Sessions.js:255). So: a class instance, but one for all sessions, not one per session.

Q3 placement and sends. The fast seat is the voice assistant by default (Sessions.js:70-80, voice_seat() :413; 'fast' chatter is the escape hatch via session-assistant.txt). voice_say (:439, called at :992 for a standalone line and :1130 from release_thought) wakes it, and it writes one {place} line per sentence: same paragraph, own paragraph, or own card (.claude/skills/voice-assistant/SKILL.md; ux/Dictate/doc/voice-assistant.md:3); the client draws it at chat.js:213 and Widget.js Thread.draw. But the trigger is the owner's quiet, not each sentence as it ends: say() holds spoken lines (hold_thought :1104) until quiet >= answer_quiet_ms 2500 ms (Sessions.js:246, :984), the mic goes off, a typed line arrives, or hold_max_ms 8000 ms passes with no quiet event; every line held in that thought goes to the voice assistant together. The SMART seat is fed by WakePolicy (WakePolicy.js:1-6, defaults :12 gap_ms 12000, every 6): one batch when the owner pauses 12 s, when a line ends in '?' or names the smart assistant, or after 6 sentences; the mic going off flushes at once (Sessions.js:1131). So: fast = a short pause (2.5 s) per thought; smart = a longer pause (12 s), a question, a name, or 6 sentences; never per sentence, never per paragraph. Knobs: gap_ms and every are settable per session through POST /api/session/settings; answer_quiet_ms is env only today.

FLASH Q1 (planning, nothing built). The raw->cleaned swap is client-side, in the first view: ext/Chat/Mic.js:510 on_revised swaps the fast assistant's cleaned text into the held item and draw_caption redraws it; await_clean (Mic.js:545) makes a send wait up to 5 s for it; take_out (Mic.js:703) then hands {text, raw} to Widget.show_out (ux/Dictate/Widget.js:800 on_out), which draws the piece, and refine_final may patch it again with the paragraphed text. So yes: it is the 'Clean transcription' setting (fast-assistant clean-up). The 'big flash' = the long raw caption shown in the draft, then replaced in place by the cleaned piece. In Chat v2 there is NO such swap: ChatV2 draws only from session.jsonl lines (ChatV2Model.fold, ext/Chat/v2/ChatV2Model.js:61), so it shows nothing until Servex writes the owner line, then the refined text replaces it.

FLASH Q2. For Chat v2 to show raw words live, a draft source must reach it: v2 never sees the mic's caption because it lives only in the page (ComposerMic.draw_caption, ext/Chat/Mic.js:206, plus the held items). Smallest fix: have ComposerMic publish its draft (raw held + box text) through the same on_out/caption hook that Widget uses (Widget.js:800) and let ChatView (ext/drawer/ChatView.js) draw it as a grey 'draft' row at the bottom of the v2 box, removed when the owner line arrives from the file (same step as settle_draft/drop_draft, Widget.js:538-545). Draw raw, not cleaned, so there is no swap flash: the final row then replaces it in the same position. It is a client-only change; nothing goes to the file.

FLASH Q3 (why a long pause may not send). Client: auto_check (Mic.js:607) returns silently if state is not listening/transcribing, if mode is manual, if the box is empty or this.tail is unset (typed words are never auto-sent), and if last_speech is stale; a second send_screen is dropped while sending_screen is true (Mic.js:621), and that flag only clears in finally after await_clean (up to 5 s wait, :627-640), so a hung clean-up/refine delays the send; also REFINE_WAIT_MS 1500 (:119). Duplicate guard: a send within DUP_WINDOW_MS of the last identical text is dropped (:686). The timer is a setInterval of CHECK_MS 250 (:444); a long pause only fires the pause send if SETTINGS.pause_send_ms/paragraph_pause_ms are >0 and the text ends a sentence for the paragraph rule. Server: a spoken line with floor:'speaking' is held (Sessions.js:984 hold_thought) and released only by a quiet event or after hold_max_ms 8000 (:1109); answer_quiet_ms 2500 gates the quiet release (:1145). If the page never reports floor quiet and the hold timer is reset by each new line, a long monologue waits until 8 s after the last line. No path drops the timer outright, but an exception in auto_check is swallowed (DictateHealth.fail, :616). Not reproduced; from code only.
